content.title: About
content.content: Ready‑to‑eat oat bran cereal is made from whole oat bran that has been dried and pressed into light flakes. It is rich in fiber, B‑vitamins, and minerals, offering a mild nutty flavor and a convenient quick‑breakfast option.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Oat bran contains more dietary fiber than regular rolled oats.
Bran is the outer layer of the oat grain that is removed during the production of standard oat flakes.
Minimal heat processing preserves most of the nutrients in ready‑to‑eat oat bran flakes.
Oats have been cultivated for over 5,000 years, making them one of the oldest grain crops.
Bran is often used in diet plans to help lower cholesterol levels.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Heart‑healthy
items.content: Beta‑glucans in bran can reduce LDL‑cholesterol, supporting cardiovascular health.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B2, and B6 aid energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: Bran provides magnesium, iron, and phosphorus, essential for bone and muscle health.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: The fiber slows carbohydrate absorption, helping control appetite and glucose spikes.

items.title: Oat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to oats or oat proteins.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Bran contains phytic acid, which can reduce the absorption of certain minerals when consumed in excess.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: A sudden increase in fiber intake may cause bloating or loose stools.

items.title: Gluten cross‑contamination
items.content: Although oats are naturally gluten‑free, they are often processed on equipment shared with wheat; choose certified gluten‑free products if you have celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy oat bran flakes dry, or add milk, yogurt, or plant‑based milk. Mix with fresh fruit, nuts, honey, or use in smoothies, baked goods, and as a topping for salads for a quick, nutritious meal.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the flakes in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from light. For longer shelf life, keep them refrigerated to prevent fat oxidation. Discard if they develop a rancid smell or visible mold.
